label: UEFN MCP (Epic)
description: Official Epic in-editor MCP nested under Ducky, in UEFN and in Unreal Editor 5.8+ (Unreal MCP). UI shows three tools: unreal__list_toolsets, unreal__describe_toolset, unreal__call_tool — then call that editor's toolsets (UEFN 43.00: ValkyrieFortniteToolset Device/Session, ValkyrieToolset.EntityToolset, VerseToolset.VerseToolset and EditorToolset.*). Ducky checks which editor holds the port and never sends island work to Unreal Editor, or Unreal project work to UEFN. Do not add a second IDE mcp.json entry.
requirements_note: Enable the island in Ducky, then open it in UEFN. Default bind http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp. In Settings → MCPs look for "UEFN MCP (Epic)" (id unreal-mcp). Do not enable a second custom HTTP MCP on the same port.
setup_steps: Enable this island in Ducky. That turns on Python and starts Epic MCP.
Open the project in UEFN (restart once if Epic MCP is still off).
In Settings → MCPs confirm "UEFN MCP (Epic)" is Enabled (slug unreal-mcp).
Do not enable another HTTP/SSE MCP on the same host:port — Ducky blocks that and will disable duplicates.
If port 8000 is taken, set Editor Preferences → Model Context Protocol port, then Settings → MCPs unreal-mcp URL to match.

Unreal Editor 5.8+: enable the Unreal MCP and All Toolsets plugins, run ModelContextProtocol.StartServer once, and open the project folder (the one with the .uproject) in Ducky. Ducky moves Unreal Editor to port 8001 with Auto Start on, so after one restart it never blocks UEFN.
